reviews.reasoning: The span is probably right and the warrant is not. Verification first: the Hebrew quote at oshb:Ps.135.5 collates at BYTE tier; 4 of 4 WEB quotes (web:Ps.135.5, web:Ps.135.6, web:Ps.135.8, web:Ps.135.11) are verbatim; the 1 verse argued outside the span, 135:13, is present in boundary_evidence_refs; Ps 135 is identity-numbered so no dual-cite is owed; pmarks_Ps.json records 0 selah verses and 0 ketiv/qere verses in Ps 135. The 12|13 seam itself is real — oshb:Ps.135.13 carries 2 second-person-singular suffixed nouns referring to Yahweh, matched by “Your name, Yahweh, endures forever; your renown, Yahweh, throughout all generations.” (web:Ps.135.13). But the row states its warrant as a person-number contrast and asserts it as a universal over the whole span, and that universal is falsified in 2 of the span's 8 verses, both of them verses the row itself cites: 135:5, which the row quotes and glosses, is first-person, and 135:9, which the row paraphrases without its addressed clause, turns to second-person address of Egypt. The arithmetic '8 of 8' is right about the verse count and wrong about the property counted — a count-object mismatch. The row also carries confidence 'high' on a discriminator that fails inside its own span, and both observed_substrate_signals and rejected_alternative repeat the same premise, so they are dependent fields of any repair.

reviews.reasoning: Support on the merits, with everything re-derived. The Hebrew quote at oshb:Ps.135.13 collates at BYTE tier. The second-person claim is byte-verifiable and correct: 135:13 carries 2 second-person-singular suffixed nouns and names Yahweh twice, and both witnesses read the 2 divine names as vocative apposition — “Your name, Yahweh, endures forever; your renown, Yahweh, throughout all generations.” (web:Ps.135.13). The reversion claim at 135:14 is likewise correct, and 2 of 2 WEB quotes on this row are verbatim, including “For Yahweh will judge his people and have compassion on his servants.” (web:Ps.135.14). Holding the couplet together is grounded in the original language beyond what the row itself says: 135:14 opens with a motive particle binding it back to 135:13, so the 2 verses are 1 syntactic movement. The selah signal is correctly formed — pmarks_Ps.json records 0 selah verses in Ps 135 out of 71 book-wide, and the row scopes the absence to its own span rather than to the psalm or the book, which is the required form. pmarks_Ps.json records 0 ketiv/qere verses in Ps 135 out of 65 book-wide, so no disclosure is owed; paseq is present in the psalm at MT 135:1, 135:9, 135:11 and 135:21 (1 seg each, seg layer, single-witness) and correctly not invoked here. Ps 135 is identity-numbered, so no dual-cite is owed. confidence 'medium_low' is honest for a 2-verse hinge whose seams are both content-marked rather than device-marked. One observation, not a challenge: 135:14 is characterised here as part of a hinge with the recital closing at 135:12, but the row governing 135:15-18 places 135:14 inside the historical recital — the 2 descriptions of the same verse cannot both stand, and the defect is filed against 135:15-18, where the misdescription is load-bearing; the cure is 1 edit installed on both sides of the seam at 135:14|15.

The span is sound and the strong half of the row's original-language comparison survives byte checking; the ground for the opening seam and 1 comparative signal do not. Name the object and the unit, then count: if the intended object is the whole inert-organ list across 115:5-7, say so and count it; as written the signal is a verse-to-verse length claim the bytes contradict.

reviews.reasoning: Support on the span and on the counts; challenge on 1 original-language label. Verified: both Hebrew quotes, at oshb:Ps.135.19 and oshb:Ps.135.20, collate at BYTE tier; 3 of 3 WEB quotes (web:Ps.135.19, web:Ps.135.20, web:Ps.135.21) are verbatim; the psalm is identity-numbered so no dual-cite is owed; pmarks_Ps.json records 0 selah verses and 0 ketiv/qere verses in Ps 135. The fourfold count is exact: the bless imperative occurs 4 times across the 2 verses 135:19-20 (unit: tokens), addressing 4 groups — house of Israel and house of Aaron at 135:19, house of Levi and the fearers of Yahweh at 135:20. The three-member comparison is arithmetically right as well: Ps 115:9-11 and Ps 118:2-4 name 3 groups each (unit: groups), and house of Levi is genuinely the added fourth. The verse-final hallelu-Yah at 135:21 is in psalm_device_inventory.json halleluyah.verse_final (13 entries book-wide), and pairing it with the verse-initial occurrences at 135:1 and 135:3 (2 of the 11 verse-initial entries) is inventory-true. One observation, not a challenge: WEB renders 2 distinct Hebrew roots with the same English verb — 3 occurrences of praise at web:Ps.135.1 render the hallel root and 4 across web:Ps.135.19-20 render the bless root — so an English-only reading of the bracket claim would see a lexical inclusio the Hebrew does not carry; the row's quoted Hebrew is what keeps the claim honest, and the claim itself is pitched at the level of imperative-plus-vocative form, which does return. What fails is the label put on the Ps 115 parallel.

challenges.evidence: All 3 psalms are identity-numbered, so web:Ps.C.V = oshb:Ps.C.V. Skeleton sweep of the bless root over each psalm's own bytes (verse_map_oshb.json; unit: tokens): Ps 115 has 5 tokens over 3 verses — 3 at 115:12, 1 at 115:13, 1 at 115:18 — of which 0 carry the imperative skeleton; Ps 135 has 4 tokens over 2 verses, 4 of 4 imperative; Ps 118 has 1 token in the whole psalm, at 118:26, 0 of them imperative. The pointed forms bear this out. Ps 135's call: בָּרֲכ֣וּ (oshb:Ps.135.19) — “House of Israel, praise Yahweh! House of Aaron, praise Yahweh!” (web:Ps.135.19). The Ps 115 passage whose membership the row names uses the trust root instead: בְּטַ֣ח (oshb:Ps.115.9) and בִּטְח֣וּ (oshb:Ps.115.10) — “Israel, trust in Yahweh! He is their help and their shield.” (web:Ps.115.9). Ps 115's blessing passage is not a call but prefix forms — יְבָ֫רֵ֥ךְ (oshb:Ps.115.12), יְ֭בָרֵךְ (oshb:Ps.115.13), נְבָ֘רֵ֤ךְ (oshb:Ps.115.18) — and its first member is בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ps.115.12): “Yahweh remembers us. He will bless us. He will bless the house of Israel. He will bless the house of Aaron.” (web:Ps.115.12). So neither Ps 115 passage matches both the root and the membership the row asserts. The count the row leans on is unaffected and correct: 3 groups in Ps 115:9-11 and 3 in Ps 118:2-4 — יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ps.118.2), בֵֽית אַהֲרֹ֑ן (oshb:Ps.118.3), יִרְאֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.118.4) — against 4 in Ps 135:19-20 (unit: groups). Name the swept object: this is a shared addressee-list, not a shared bless-formula, and the row's own label for Ps 118, a call-and-response, is the accurate kind.
